sources.citation: Sato, Hiroko. 2016. Akolet. In Simon J. Greenhill, Robert Blust & Russell D. Gray (eds.), Austronesian Basic Vocabulary Database, language id 1395 (source: 'Hiroko Sato, 2016, personal communication'; data entry and checking Kwang-Ju Cho; source field edited by Malcolm Ross 2017-09-13). 223 entries (210-meaning list). Also redistributed as Lexibank abvdoceanic 'Akolet_1395' and, in 40-item form, as the ASJP AKOLET list.
sources.note: Nothing. All 223 items are in plain roman orthography (digraphs ng, gh; w, y; no diacritics: a scan of the CSV finds zero non-ASCII characters and zero stress/accent marks). The 'Notes' field of the language record is empty. The 56 annotations are semantic or grammatical only, e.g. 'he/she: pa (unmarried M), som (married M), et (unmarried F), eng (married F)'; 'we: aiet (incl), aiem (excl)'; 'they: wol (unmarried M & F), nowk (married M), min (married F)'; 'to hunt: yung (this is a noun and means hunting with dogs)'. Sample forms: lama 'hand', kinken 'leg/foot', mata 'eye', langalo 'ear', hot…

sources.note: No phonology of A Kolet/Arawe beyond one segmental-historical remark (p.371: 'Like the Pasismanua and Lamogai Families, as well as Kilenge-Maleu, Arawe shows a strong tendency for *a of PAN forms to shift to e or i.. Arawe is unique in having such forms as nimo hand and moto eye'). The only prosodic remark in the chapter concerns other families: p.380 fn. 'There are a few suggestive resemblances, including the possibility of phonemic tone in some Whiteman languages'. Nothing on stress or accent for any Arawe language.
